coreRule: Every NPC that exists in canon has a mechanical sheet. Named/recurring NPCs receive dedicated sheets immediately. Incidental NPCs instantiate from a complete archetype sheet and become permanently unique the moment they acquire a name, consequential memory, relationship, quest role, or recurring relevance.

rules: NPCs gain XP for meaningful goals advanced, dangerous encounters survived, significant discoveries, training, social victories, sacrifices and consequential failures.
Never rubber-band NPC level to the player.
Off-screen accomplishments can award XP when supported by plan, ability, time and opportunity.
Level-up choices follow demonstrated behavior and growthWeights, not optimal-build omniscience.
Level-ups may improve max resources, one attribute at milestone levels, relevant skills, a trait, spell/ritual access, equipment competence or social/faction capability.

alignmentModel.note: Labels such as pragmatic good or lawful zealot are shorthand only. Decisions use the numeric axes plus goals and memories.

memoryModel.intensity: 1-5; 4-5 memories rarely decay and strongly influence decisions
memoryModel.confidence: 0-100; supports mistaken, manipulated or uncertain memories without making NPC omniscient
rules: NPCs remember mercy, humiliation, debts, promises, lies, public reputation, theft, wounds, rescue, abandonment and witnessed competence.
A memory must affect future behavior when one of its behaviorHooks is relevant.
NPC knowledge and NPC memory are separate: remembering that Rook lied does not reveal what the truth was.
High-intensity identity, betrayal, death and true-name memories do not silently expire.
Memories may be falsified only through an explicit world effect or established memory magic.

hardRules: NPCs cannot act on information absent from their knowledge ledger.
NPCs can refuse Rook, lie, leave, betray, bargain, flee, attack, change allegiance or pursue goals off-screen.
NPC behavior must remain mechanically plausible given travel time, resources and injuries.
Consequential choices write a memory and usually alter at least one relationship/goal/plan field.

offscreenSimulation.resultLimit: Resolve only actors materially affected by the trigger. Do not simulate the whole population.
